mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate future rate cuts and lower borrowing costs.
regime_hint: Protracted monetary tightening or holding pattern
failure_condition: Over 18 months, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform a 2% risk-free rate benchmark in the same period (Sharpe ratio < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 50,000 jobs in the prior month is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals labor market resilience and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: Across 30 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a 0.5% risk-free rate (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) show double-digit month-over-month growth simultaneously, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting strong aggregate demand.
regime_hint: Concurrent strong supply and demand indicators
failure_condition: In 50 such double-digit growth events, the 20-day forward returns do not beat a 1% risk-free benchmark (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% in the prior month predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it signals weakening manufacturing momentum and reduced investment.
failure_condition: Over 12 INDPRO contractions exceeding 5%, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically worse than random chance (Granger causality p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weak labor market absorption and risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0 and UNRATE > prev_month and UNRATE > month_before_prev_month
failure_condition: Across 15 such UNRATE regimes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) prints a monthly YoY increase above 3% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2%, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting inflation surprise versus policy restraint.
regime_hint: Inflation surprise in a restrictive policy environment
failure_condition: In 20 such inflation-surprise/restrictive-policy events, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform a 1.5% inflation-protected risk-free rate (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a 2% monthly rise in GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) and a 10% monthly increase in PAYEMS predicts a positive S&P 5-day forward return, capturing near-term consumption and labor momentum.
regime_hint: Short-term consumption and labor momentum acceleration
failure_condition: Across 40 such events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
